title: L'attente au café  (Waiting at the Café)

segments.t: Sitting anxiously at a bistro table, Andrea waits for her important meeting with iconic actress Nathalie Baye. When she orders another coffee, a playful waiter teases her with celebrity lookalikes until an urgent phone call reveals that Mathias has diverted Nathalie to ASK. Let's listen to their conversation in French first.
Pardon monsieur, excusez-moi.
Oui madame, que désirez-vous?
Je peux commander un autre café?
Bien sûr, je vous l'apporte immédiatement.
Vous avez vu Nathalie Baye aujourd'hui?
Nathalie Baye? Non, pas du tout.
Mais Catherine Deneuve est assise là-bas!
Vraiment? Où ça dans la salle?
Je plaisante, c'était une petite blague!
Super, je n'ai pas le temps de rire.
Allô Gabriel? Où est passée Nathalie?
Mathias l'a emmenée directement à l'agence!
Madame, voici votre nouveau café chaud!
Donnez-le plutôt à Catherine Deneuve!
Let's examine the conversation line by line and explore the French expressions.
Pardon monsieur, excusez-moi.
'Pardon sir, excuse me.' Andrea calls the waiter to her table. The polite formulas 'pardon' and 'excuse me' request attention.
Oui madame, que désirez-vous?
'Yes madam, what would you like?' The waiter responds with professional courtesy. The formal question 'que desirez-vous' asks for an order.
Je peux commander un autre café?
'Can I order another coffee?' Andrea asks for another drink while waiting. The modal verb 'can' expresses permission to place an order.
Bien sûr, je vous l'apporte immédiatement.
'Of course, I bring it to you immediately.' The waiter confirms the second cup. The adverb 'immediately' signals prompt service.
Vous avez vu Nathalie Baye aujourd'hui?
'Have you seen Nathalie Baye today?' Andrea checks whether her actress has arrived. The passe compose 'have' asks about past visual sighting.
Nathalie Baye? Non, pas du tout.
'Nathalie Baye? No, not at all.' The waiter clarifies that he has not spotted her. The negative phrase 'not at all' means not in the least.
Mais Catherine Deneuve est assise là-bas!
'But Catherine Deneuve is seated over there!' The waiter points out a playful illusion. The past participle 'seated' functions here as a predicate adjective.
Vraiment? Où ça dans la salle?
'Really? Where in the room?' Andrea takes the bait for a brief moment. The question 'where' asks for a specific location.
Je plaisante, c'était une petite blague!
'I am joking, it was a little joke!' The waiter laughs at his own jest. The verb 'am joking' means to joke or kid.
Super, je n'ai pas le temps de rire.
'Great, I do not have time to laugh.' Andrea shows her impatience under pressure. The noun phrase 'not' denotes lack of available time.
Allô Gabriel? Où est passée Nathalie?
'Hello Gabriel? Where did Nathalie go?' Andrea checks in by phone. The interjection 'hello' begins French telephone calls.
Mathias l'a emmenée directement à l'agence!
'Mathias took her directly to the agency!' Andrea learns of Mathias's tactical maneuver. The compound passe compose 'a emmenee' describes accompanying someone somewhere.
Madame, voici votre nouveau café chaud!
'Madam, here is your hot fresh coffee!' The waiter delivers the cup as she rises. The presentation adverb 'here is' presents an item directly.
Donnez-le plutôt à Catherine Deneuve!

'Give it instead to Catherine Deneuve!' Andrea snaps back with dry sarcasm. The adverb 'rather' means instead or rather. Now let's listen to the complete discussion once more to reinforce the vocabulary.
Pardon monsieur, excusez-moi.
Oui madame, que désirez-vous?
Je peux commander un autre café?
Bien sûr, je vous l'apporte immédiatement.
Vous avez vu Nathalie Baye aujourd'hui?
Nathalie Baye? Non, pas du tout.
Mais Catherine Deneuve est assise là-bas!
Vraiment? Où ça dans la salle?
Je plaisante, c'était une petite blague!
Super, je n'ai pas le temps de rire.
Allô Gabriel? Où est passée Nathalie?
Mathias l'a emmenée directement à l'agence!
Madame, voici votre nouveau café chaud!
Donnez-le plutôt à Catherine Deneuve!

Andrea races out of the cafe after realizing Mathias has intercepted Nathalie Baye. Leaving the waiter with his coffee joke, she rushes to the agency to regain control of the situation. Now, let's review the scene one last time.
Donnez-le plutôt à Catherine Deneuve!
